subject: LucidBank: request for full subprocessor snapshot and country-chain egress playbook
messages:
From: Asha Patel <procurement@lucidbank.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@lucidbank.com
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Subprocessor inventory + egress playbook request

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick call earlier. As part of our final procurement checklist we need a current inventory of Redwood's subprocessors that touch customer data for hosted inference (summary by role), and — critically — a simple egress/cross-border chain for data leaving the EU/UK/US. Our legal team also asked for a short "egress playbook" describing what happens if an intermediate processor is decommissioned (who's responsible for exports, timelines, and evidence we'd receive).

Can you please provide:
- A CSV with processors, country of operations, encryption-at-rest/transit notes, and whether they handle logs or telemetry.
- A brief document (1–2 pages) that outlines the egress chain and the emergency decommission playbook.
- Any supporting evidence (SOC2 scope indicator or attestations) you can share now.

We need this for our vendor committee on Thursday (30 Dec). Appreciate quick turnaround — if there are things you can't share publicly we can sign an NDA/update DPA.

Best,
Asha
Procurement Manager
LucidBank

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <procurement@lucidbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 12:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor inventory + egress playbook request

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the note and the timeline. Attaching a fresh inventory export (redwood_subprocessor_inventory_v20261229.csv) and a one-page draft egress playbook (egress_chain_playbook_draft_v1.docx). The CSV includes country, role, handles-logs flag, and our encryption notes.

A few quick clarifications up front:
- The CSV marks transient telemetry processors separately from those that persist content.
- For decommission events our standard process is: 1) notify customers 30 days in advance unless emergency; 2) provide export snapshots and checksums; 3) escrow evidence on request (can be via signed DPA addendum).

Kimberly and Marissa — I’ve looped you for legal/procurement redlines and to confirm what evidence package we can share with LucidBank pre-DPA signature.

Asha — if you need certified artifacts (SOC2 report) we can route that via our security team under an NDA — happy to expedite.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Onboarding, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_inventory_v20261229.csv; egress_chain_playbook_draft_v1.docx

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 08:17:00 -08:00
Subject: FW: LucidBank request — verify sharing scope and evidence

Folks —

Quick internal: Stephanie attached a draft inventory and playbook. Two items I want confirmed before we send any SOC2-related artifacts:
1) Are any of the processors listed US-cloud-hosted subsidiaries of third parties (we need to flag cross-border escrow complexity).
2) Which processors are within our "limited-access" observability pipeline (we only provide aggregated telemetry for customers unless they have an approved DPA addendum).

Jonas — can you validate the egress chain language in the playbook and confirm the export timeline we typically offer for emergency decommissions? I recall the standard is 30 days with an expedited 72-hour snapshot option for paid Dedicated customers, but we need to be explicit for procurement.

Marissa — if LucidBank asks for SOC2 summary or a redacted report, route them to security@redwood.ai and propose an NDA/attestation flow; avoid sending full PDFs without an approved request.

I’ll prepare a one-paragraph cover note that clarifies what we can provide pre-DPA.

-Kimberly
VP, Legal and Privacy

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <procurement@lucidbank.com>, LucidBank Security Team <security@lucidbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 15:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor inventory + egress playbook request — Redwood response

Hi Asha —

Appreciate the urgency; please find the items attached and summarized below. We kept the initial package intentionally high-level to avoid sharing certified artifacts before an NDA/DPA is in place. If the committee needs SOC2 scope verification we can provide a redacted SOC2 summary through our security team within 24 hours of an NDA.

Summary (attachments):
- redwood_subprocessor_inventory_v20261229.csv — current list (role, country, handles-logs true/false, encryption notes).
- egress_chain_playbook_draft_v1.docx — 1.5 pages: chain diagram, responsible owners, timelines (standard 30-day notice, 72-hour expedited snapshot for Dedicated with export fee), and evidence types.
- luci dbank_egress_map_request_form.pdf — form to capture which account-level exports they need (attached for their legal team).

Keynotes:
- Any SOC2 or full-report artifacts: route to security@redwood.ai, requires an official request (NDA/DPA addendum).
- For emergency decommission: we provide snapshots, MD5 checksums, and a signed delivery attestation. We own data orchestration and will coordinate with the affected subprocessor for exports unless that subprocessor is subject to third-party export restrictions — we flag that in the CSV.

Next steps: please confirm whether the committee wants the redacted SOC2 summary or is comfortable proceeding with the package we sent. Happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk through the CSV and playbook this afternoon.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Onboarding, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_inventory_v20261229.csv; egress_chain_playbook_draft_v1.docx; lucidbank_egress_map_request_form.pdf
